newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: New recycling method seen boosting scrap aluminium.
newsitem.headline: New recycling method seen boosting scrap aluminium.

text.p: Scrap aluminium prices could rise sharply following the development by Dutch scientists of an improved recycling technique, the Delft University of Technology said.
The new technique can mechanically separate 90 percent of all aluminium scrap from cars and building sites, the university said in a statement on Friday.

"Aluminium recycled in that way has a higher purity level and therefore needs less energy for re-use in new products," it said. "It is expected that the price of scrap aluminium will increase considerably once the method is implemented."

Recycled aluminium consists of casting aluminium alloy and the more expensive wrought aluminium alloy and up until now it has only been possible to separate small quantities of the two types by hand, and with only limited levels of purity.

But scientists at the university, using videocameras and image-processing techniques, have developed a system that when linked to a mechanical separator "can easily recycle at a rate a hundred times higher than manual separation, combined with a much higher level of purity," the university said.

In the auto industry, casting aluminium alloys, which contain silicon, are used in brakes, engines and door handles. Wrought aluminium alloys, which have a little magnesium mixed in, are used for trims, number plates and bumpers.
